_comment: How to tell each animal apart, shown in the review window next to its reference photos. Only marks that are reliable and visible on a camera; left out when unsure.

marks.blacksmith: Dark blue-gray with black spots toward the tail; forked tail; hangs in schools. Young ones are two-tone, bluish in front and yellowish behind.
marks.senorita: Small, slim, cigar-shaped and yellow to orange, with a black spot at the base of the tail.
marks.garibaldi: Bright orange all over. Young ones are orange-red with bright blue spots.
marks.kelp bass: Olive-brown with pale blotches along the back; big mouth. Also called calico bass.
marks.barred sand bass: Gray-brown with dark bars down the sides; stays near the bottom by sand.
marks.giant sea bass: Huge and dark gray. Young ones are orange-red with black spots.
marks.opaleye: Oval and olive-green with blue-green eyes; usually one or two white spots on the back.
marks.halfmoon: Oval and blue-gray, darker above; a crescent-shaped tail.
marks.zebra-perch sea chub: Oval and gray with dark vertical bars and a blue spot on the gill cover.
marks.California sheephead: Males: black head and tail, red middle, white chin. Females: pinkish-red all over. Buck teeth.
marks.rock wrasse: A slim wrasse like a senorita, but bigger and olive to brown, without the black spot at the tail. Males have a dark bar behind the head.
marks.black perch: Dark brown to bluish-black surfperch, often with faint bars; a patch of big scales near the pectoral fin.
marks.pile perch: Silvery-gray surfperch with one dark bar across the middle of the side; long front rays on the soft dorsal fin.
marks.rubberlip seaperch: Large, pale surfperch with thick white to pinkish lips.
marks.walleye surfperch: Silvery, with big eyes and black tips on the pelvic fins; schools.
marks.shiner perch: Small and silvery with rows of dark dots and faint yellow bars.
marks.white seaperch: Silvery, with a black line along the base of the soft dorsal fin; forked tail.
marks.barred surfperch: Silvery with rusty bars and spots; over sand in the surf.
marks.kelp perch: Small, slender, tan to coppery surfperch with an upturned snout; in the kelp.
marks.rainbow surfperch: Striped orange-red and blue, with blue bars on the head.
marks.salema: Silvery with orange-brown stripes along the side and big eyes; schools.
marks.sargo: Silvery-gray with one dark bar running down from the front of the dorsal fin.
marks.topsmelt: Slim with a bright silver stripe along the side; hard to tell from jacksmelt on camera (the silversides group is fine).
marks.jacksmelt: Slim with a bright silver stripe along the side; hard to tell from topsmelt on camera (the silversides group is fine).
marks.California grunion: Slim with a silver stripe, like topsmelt; hard to tell apart on camera (the silversides group is fine).
marks.northern anchovy: Small and silvery-green with an overhanging snout and a huge mouth; dense schools.
marks.Pacific sardine: Silvery with a row of dark spots along the side; schools.
marks.Pacific barracuda: Long and slender with a pointed, jutting lower jaw.
marks.Pacific chub mackerel: Streamlined, with wavy dark lines on a green back.
marks.jack mackerel: Streamlined, with a row of hard scales along the whole lateral line.
marks.Pacific bonito: Streamlined, with dark slanted stripes on the back.
marks.yellowtail amberjack: Silvery with a yellow stripe along the side and a yellow tail.
marks.California corbina: Slender and gray-blue with one barbel on the chin; feeds on sand in the surf.
marks.spotfin croaker: A clear black spot at the base of the pectoral fin.
marks.yellowfin croaker: Yellow fins and dark wavy lines along the sides.
marks.giant kelpfish: Long and slender with a long dorsal fin and pointed snout; colored like the kelp it hides in.
marks.kelp rockfish: Mottled brown-olive rockfish that rests motionless in kelp.
marks.tubesnout: Very thin with a long tube-like snout; tiny spines along the back.
marks.California scorpionfish: Mottled red-brown with a spiny head; sits still on the bottom. Venomous spines.
marks.cabezon: Big head, mottled skin; sits on the bottom.
marks.painted greenling: Small, with red-brown bands around the body; perches on rock.
marks.California lizardfish: Slender with a lizard-like head; sits on sand propped on its fins.
marks.California moray eel: Long brown-green eel, usually just the head out of a crevice, mouth opening and closing.
marks.California halibut: Flatfish on sand with a big, toothy mouth; the lateral line arches over the pectoral fin.
marks.speckled sanddab: Small flatfish, tan with dark speckles.
marks.bullseye pufferfish: Rounded body that can puff up; dark spots and rings on the back.
marks.finescale triggerfish: Tall, oval and gray-brown with a small mouth.
marks.leopard shark: Slender gray shark with black saddles and spots across the back.
marks.horn shark: Blunt head, ridges above the eyes, and a spine in front of each dorsal fin.
marks.shovelnose guitarfish: Flat front with a shovel-shaped snout and a shark-like tail.
marks.banded guitarfish: Like a shovelnose guitarfish, with dark bands across the back.
marks.bat ray: Big wings, a raised head and a long thin tail.
marks.round stingray: Small round disc with a short, thick tail; lies on sand.
marks.diamond stingray: Diamond-shaped disc with a long whip-like tail.
marks.California spiny lobster: Reddish-brown with very long antennae and no big claws. Here often only its antennae, sweeping from the top of the near piling.
marks.octopus: Two-spot octopus: a blue eyespot below each eye.
marks.sheep crab: Big spider crab with long legs, often covered in growth.
marks.yellow rock crab: Wide oval shell, yellow-orange, with black-tipped claws.
marks.giant spined sea star: Large sea star with big white spines on a brown to orange body.
marks.bat star: Webbed, short-armed sea star in many colors.
marks.California sea hare: Large, soft reddish-brown sea slug with ear-like tentacles.
marks.black sea nettle jellyfish: Huge dark purple bell with long ribbon-like arms.
marks.purple-striped jellyfish: Pale bell with purple stripes radiating from the top.
marks.Pacific sea nettle jellyfish: Golden-brown bell with long thin tentacles.
marks.moon jellyfish: Clear saucer-shaped bell with four rings in the middle.
marks.green sea turtle: Sea turtle with a smooth shell and a small, rounded head.
marks.pelagic red crab: Small bright red lobster-like crab, in swarms.
marks.market squid: Small squid with big eyes, often in groups.
marks.California sea lion: Dark brown with small ear flaps; swims with its front flippers.
marks.harbor seal: Spotted gray with a round head and no ear flaps.
marks.diving cormorant: Black bird swimming underwater, pushing with its feet.
